faqs.q: How does salary sacrifice work with my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice allows you to exchange part of your pre-tax salary for benefits like extra super contributions or a car. It reduces your taxable income, but it is not included in this estimate. Your annual gross is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, before any salary sacrifice arrangements. For a detailed explanation, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the base rate set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries or occupations, set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This calculator uses your entered hourly rate, which may be an award rate or above. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading on top of the base rate. See our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for more.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Tax is estimated using the 2026–27 resident tax scale: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy of 2% applies to most taxpayers. This estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For more details, visit our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have received a salary offer, understanding your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. This guide explains how to convert your hourly rate to annual gross pay using a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year. We also cover the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax. And if you are wondering **how does salary sacrifice work**, we touch on that too.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours worked per week × 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, the calculation is:

Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52 = hourly rate × 1,976.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross is $30.00 × 1,976 = $59,280. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. Using the same $30.00 per hour example:

Weekly gross = $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
Fortnightly gross = $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00

This can help you budget and compare with salary offers expressed per fortnight.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

We assume a 38-hour week because that is the standard full-time week under the Fair Work Act. However, some awards or agreements may specify different hours. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the formula accordingly. Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your own hours.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Many employees are covered by awards that set higher minimum rates for their industry or role. This calculator does not assume a specific award; you enter your actual hourly rate. If you are unsure, check your award or agreement via the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog).

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. In our calculator, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. This matches the National Minimum Wage casual rate from 1 July 2026. Learn more on our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

### Superannuation – Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. The rate is 12% for the 2026–27 year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to your employer. In our estimate, super is calculated as 12% of your ordinary earnings (hourly rate × hours worked) and stops once earnings exceed the cap. For example, on $59,280 annual gross, the super contribution would be $59,280 × 0.12 = $7,113.60, paid on top. This is not included in your take-home pay. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for more.

### How Does Salary Sacrifice Work?

Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you agree to forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as additional super contributions, a car, or electronic devices. It reduces your taxable income, which may lower the tax you pay. However, salary sacrifice is **not included** in this basic annual pay estimate. The formula here assumes your full hourly rate is paid as cash wages. If you salary sacrifice, your actual cash pay will be lower, but your total remuneration package may include the sacrificed benefits. For a detailed explanation, visit our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Tax is estimated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. We use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate. This estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or any tax offsets. For a more personalised calculation, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Example Calculation

Let’s say you earn $35.00 per hour, work 38 hours per week, and are permanent full-time (no casual loading).

- Weekly gross: $35.00 × 38 = $1,330.00
- Fortnightly gross: $1,330.00 × 2 = $2,660.00
- Annual gross: $35.00 × 1,976 = $69,160.00
- Super (12%): $69,160.00 × 0.12 = $8,299.20 (paid on top)
- Estimated tax (2026–27): $18,200 tax-free, then $45,000 – $18,200 = $26,800 at 15% = $4,020, then $69,160 – $45,000 = $24,160 at 30% = $7,248. Total tax = $11,268. Plus Medicare levy 2% = $1,383.20. Total deductions = $12,651.20. Estimated annual take-home = $69,160 – $12,651.20 = $56,508.80.

This is an estimate only. Actual pay may vary due to leave, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated super and tax. It is a quick way to see how your hourly rate translates to different pay periods.

### Important Notes

- This estimate assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave.
- It does not include penalty rates, overtime, allowances, or bonuses.
- Salary sacrifice is not factored in – if you want to understand **how does salary sacrifice work** in your situation, consult a tax professional or the Australian Taxation Office.
- The National Minimum Wage and award rates are minimums; your actual rate may be higher.
- Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings and does not reduce your cash pay.

For more detailed information, see our [reference tables](/data) or [average pay](/topics/average-pay) pages. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026 – that is an average across all industries, not a median for your specific job. Always check your award or agreement for your correct rate.
